text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen is unperturbed by the decision of a majority in the leadership of the opposition far-left Socialist Peoples Party to recommend a "no" to the European Union's Amsterdam Treaty at an extraordinary party conference in September. Danes are to vote on the issue in a referendum next year.
--For the first time in 15 years Copenhagen Council is in a position to present a balanced budget without having to resort to local tax rises.

--Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) Cargo is actively beefing up its freight services to the Far East in an effort to increase its share in a lucrative market. SAS Cargo plans to extend freight routes to the Far East by 20 percent, increasing flights to Macau from the current two to three a week, each Boeing 747 plane having a capacity for 100 tonnes cargo. SAS Cargo wants to up earnings by 100 million crowns annually.
--Denmark's booming windmill/wind turbine industry sold 74 percent more units in 1997's first six months than in the same 1996 period.

--Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) has joint venture plans in Japan for next year and has reportedly found a local partner in Asia's biggest and most demanding market. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
